chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr, from 'Asim, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment regarding a man whose one eye had been injured: that an ostrich egg should be taken and he should be made to walk with it, and his sound eye should be bound so that he does not see it, until the limit of his sight is reached. Then the difference between the limit of sight of his injured eye and the limit of his sound eye should be calculated, and compensation should be paid according to that calculation.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam 'Ali عليه السلام in his authority as leader and judge
key_terms.بَيْضَةُ نَعَامَةٍ: an ostrich egg used here as a means of testing visual range
key_terms.بِحِسَابِ ذَلِكَ: according to that calculation or measured proportion
key_terms.فَيُؤَدَّى: then payment is to be rendered
key_terms.قَضَى: gave judgment or issued a legal ruling

ai.seo_question: How did Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام rule on compensation for injury to one eye?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning compensation for partial loss of sight in one eye. It describes a practical method for measuring visual impairment so that the diyah may be assessed proportionately and justly.
